papers.title: DBAASP V4: condition-resolved bioactivity and chemical structures for data-driven peptide and peptidomimetic discovery.
papers.abstract: The current peptide renaissance-driven by metagenomic and proteomic mining, molecular de-extinction, protein language models, and generative or evolutionary design-is producing millions of candidates, but useful machine learning depends on experimentally anchored, context-rich labels. The Database of Antimicrobial Activity and Structure of Peptides (DBAASP) is a manually curated resource linking peptides and peptidomimetics to quantitative antimicrobial, antibiofilm, anticancer, hemolytic, and mammalian-cell cytotoxicity measurements and their experimental conditions. DBAASP v4 contains >25 00
papers.summary: DBAASP v4 is a manually curated database that links peptides and peptidomimetics to quantitative bioactivity measurements (antimicrobial, antibiofilm, anticancer, hemolytic, cytotoxicity) along with the experimental conditions under which they were measured. With over 25,000 entries, it provides context-rich, experimentally anchored labels needed to train machine-learning models for peptide and peptidomimetic discovery.

papers.title: PROTAC-DB 4.0: an expanded knowledgebase of targeted protein degradation modalities with AI-powered knowledge discovery.
papers.abstract: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) represent an emerging therapeutic modality that harnesses the ubiquitin-proteasome system to induce targeted protein degradation (TPD). Their event-driven and catalytic mechanisms provide new opportunities to target previously undruggable proteins. However, the rapid expansion of TPD technologies, including molecular glues (MGs) and X-functional targeting chimeras (XTACs), together with the increasing application of artificial intelligence (AI) in degrader design, highlights the need for comprehensive and continuously updated data resources. Here, we pr
papers.summary: PROTAC-DB 4.0 is an updated knowledgebase that now covers not only PROTACs but also other targeted protein degradation modalities such as molecular glues and XTACs, and it incorporates AI-driven tools for knowledge discovery. The resource aims to keep pace with the rapid growth of degrader design by providing comprehensive, continuously updated data for researchers.

papers.title: dictyBase 2026: a reimplementation of the Dictyostelium model organism database on minimal infrastructure.
papers.abstract: Dictyostelium discoideum is a model organism used to investigate a wide array of biological processes including chemotaxis, cell motility, phagocytosis, multicellular development, and autophagy. Many of its genes have human orthologs implicated in disease, making it a useful model organism for studying conditions ranging from cancer to neurodegeneration. dictyBase has served this community for two decades as a home for genomic data, protocols, a stock center, and community news. Here we describe a complete reimplementation of dictyBase as a self-contained service that uses static data files ra
papers.summary: dictyBase, the long-running model organism database for Dictyostelium discoideum, has been completely reimplemented as a self-contained service built on static data files and minimal infrastructure. This redesign preserves the community's access to genomic data, protocols, stock center information, and news while reducing maintenance burden. It offers a practical template for sustaining small model organism databases with limited resources.

papers.title: Assessment of LLMs on basic bioinformatics tasks requiring multi-step reasoning and code writing.
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs), AI agents and co-scientists promise to accelerate scientific discovery across fields ranging from chemistry to biology. Bioinformatics- the analysis of DNA, RNA and protein sequences plays a crucial role in biological research and is especially amenable to AI-driven automation given its computational nature. Here, we assess the bioinformatics capabilities of popular general-purpose LLMs on a set of tasks covering basic analytical questions that include code writing and multi-step reasoning in the domain.
papers.summary: This study evaluates how well popular general-purpose large language models handle basic bioinformatics tasks that require both writing code and multi-step reasoning. The authors find that while LLMs show promise, their performance on these practical analytical problems is limited, highlighting gaps before they can be reliably used for automated bioinformatics.

papers.title: Integrative taxonomy using traits and genomic data for Species Delimitation with Deep learning.
papers.abstract: Delimiting species boundaries in complex speciation scenarios, including those involving gene flow and demographic fluctuations, remains a challenge, particularly given the diversity of existing species concepts. Promising recent approaches adopt an integrative taxonomy that combines multiple sources of evidence (e.g., genetic, morphology, geographic distributions), reflecting different properties associated with the dynamics of the speciation continuum. The use of statistical inference methods for model comparison, such as approximate Bayesian computation, approximate likelihood approaches, a
papers.summary: The paper proposes a deep learning approach for species delimitation that integrates multiple data types—genomic, morphological, and geographic—within an integrative taxonomy framework. This addresses the difficulty of distinguishing species boundaries in complex speciation scenarios involving gene flow and demographic fluctuations, where traditional single-source methods struggle. The method aims to provide a more robust statistical inference tool for model comparison than existing approximate Bayesian computation or likelihood approaches.

papers.title: Microbiome science needs AI competence, not just AI literacy.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly becoming embedded in microbiome research, yet the way microbiome scientists are trained has not kept pace. Existing discussions frequently emphasize AI literacy and responsible tool use. We argue that literacy alone is insufficient in a field where data leakage, incomplete metadata, ecological confounding, inappropriate model selection and unverified generative-AI outputs can produce convincing but biologically misleading conclusions. We propose an AI-competence framework comprising five connected capabilities: data and platform fluency, machine-learning comp
papers.summary: The authors argue that microbiome researchers need deeper AI competence—not just basic literacy—because common pitfalls like data leakage, incomplete metadata, ecological confounding, and unverified generative-AI outputs can yield plausible but biologically wrong conclusions. They propose a five-part AI-competence framework covering data/platform fluency, machine-learning competency, and related skills to guide training in the field.

papers.title: Free-breathing Pulmonary Relaxometry at 0.55T.
papers.abstract: To evaluate the feasibility of an integrated, free-breathing workflow for automated 2D pulmonary relaxometry (T1, T2) at 0.55T.
papers.summary: This study evaluates the feasibility of an integrated free-breathing workflow for automated 2D pulmonary relaxometry (T1 and T2 mapping) at 0.55T MRI. The work demonstrates that quantitative lung MRI can be performed without breath-holding at low field strength, potentially improving accessibility and patient comfort.

papers.title: Deep Lineage: Single-cell lineage tracing and fate inference using deep learning.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in single-cell RNA sequencing and lineage tracing techniques have provided valuable insights into the temporal changes in gene expression during development, tumor progression, and disease onset. However, there are few computational methods available to analyze this information to help understand multicellular dynamics. We introduce Deep Lineage, a deep-learning method for analyzing time-series single-cell RNA sequencing with matched lineage tracing data. Our method accurately predicts early cell fate biases and gene expression profiles at different time points within a clone,
papers.summary: Deep Lineage is a deep-learning method that analyzes time-series single-cell RNA sequencing data combined with matched lineage tracing to model how cells change over time. It accurately predicts early biases in cell fate and gene expression profiles at different time points within a clone, helping researchers understand multicellular dynamics in development, tumor progression, and disease.

papers.title: pdb2reaction: End-to-End Reaction-Path Elucidation from PDB Structures Using Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials.
papers.abstract: Elucidating enzymatic reaction mechanisms requires a sequence of computational tasks comprising active-site extraction, minimum-energy-path search, transition-state (TS) refinement, intrinsic reaction coordinate (IRC) validation, and quasi-rigid-rotor harmonic-oscillator (QRRHO) thermochemistrystages typically connected by ad hoc scripting and per-system tuning. We present pdb2reaction, an open-source Python command-line toolkit that automates this entire pipeline directly from a user-curated PDB using a single machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP) backend. A GPU-accelerated pysisyphu
papers.summary: pdb2reaction is an open-source Python command-line toolkit that automates the full enzymatic reaction-mechanism pipeline—active-site extraction, minimum-energy-path search, transition-state refinement, IRC validation, and QRRHO thermochemistry—starting directly from a user-curated PDB file using a single machine-learning interatomic potential backend. It replaces ad hoc scripting and per-system tuning with a unified, GPU-accelerated workflow.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Protein Secondary-Structure Segmentation in Intermediate-Resolution Cryo-EM Maps: A Resolution-Stratified Benchmark Dataset and Controlled Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Accurate segmentation of protein secondary structures in cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) maps is crucial for protein tracing and atomic model building, yet remains challenging at intermediate resolutions. Although deep learning architectures have recently been applied to this task, there remains a lack of standardized evaluation protocols and systematic resolution-stratified analyses. Consequently, it remains unclear how segmentation performance varies across finer resolution ranges within the intermediate-resolution regime and how different volumetric segmentation architectures compare und
papers.summary: This paper introduces a resolution-stratified benchmark dataset and controlled evaluation protocol for deep learning-based segmentation of protein secondary structures in intermediate-resolution cryo-EM maps. It systematically compares volumetric segmentation architectures across finer resolution ranges, addressing the lack of standardized evaluation in this regime. The work aims to clarify how segmentation performance varies with resolution and architecture choice.

papers.title: OmniVira: a knowledgebase of source-linked evidence on viral spillover and cross-species transmission.
papers.abstract: Zoonotic viral emergence poses persistent challenges to global health, yet evidence relevant to spillover and cross-species transmission is dispersed across surveillance, epidemiological, experimental, mechanistic, and genomic studies. Here, we present OmniVira (https://omnivira.org/), a curated knowledgebase that transforms literature-derived findings into structured, traceable, and reusable OmniVira Evidence (OVE) records. OmniVira implements an auditable article-evidence framework linking individual findings and supporting text to normalized virus, host, and geographic entities, and relevan
papers.summary: OmniVira is a curated knowledgebase that converts literature on viral spillover and cross-species transmission into structured, traceable evidence records. Each finding is linked to its source text and normalized virus, host, and geographic entities, making dispersed surveillance, epidemiological, and genomic evidence reusable and auditable.

papers.title: Deep Learning-Augmented Stimulated Raman Imaging for Cell-Type-Specific Metabolic Profiling in Live Neuronal Cocultures.
papers.abstract: Neuronal metabolism is fundamental to brain functions and diseases, yet its spatial and temporal dynamics and interactions remain poorly understood. Here, we introduce a tandem deep-learning approach integrated with bioorthogonal chemical imaging using stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy. This method achieves high-speed and quantitative metabolic profiling in live neuronal cocultures. Our deep-learning framework consists of a recurrent convolutional neural network (RCNN) that enables high-resolution 3D imaging with minimal photodamage and a U-Net segmentation model for cell-type-speci
papers.summary: The authors combine stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy with bioorthogonal chemical imaging and a tandem deep-learning pipeline to profile metabolism in live neuronal cocultures. A recurrent convolutional network enables high-resolution 3D imaging with reduced photodamage, while a U-Net model segments cell types so that metabolic signals can be assigned to specific cells. This provides a label-free, cell-type-specific view of metabolic dynamics in living neurons.

papers.title: Prediction of Residue-Level Base Preference for DNA-Binding Proteins Using a Multimodal Learning Framework.
papers.abstract: Specific recognition between proteins and DNA governs essential cellular functions, yet the binding specificity of most DNA-binding proteins (DBPs) remains experimentally uncharacterized and high-throughput experimental methods still lag far behind the ever-growing protein data set. Here, we present 3M-BSIP (3-modal base-specific interaction predictor), a multimodal deep learning framework capable of predicting the DNA-binding interface and residue-level base preference for DBPs. 3M-BSIP constructs a holistic protein representation by integrating three distinct modalities: a protein language m
papers.summary: The authors present 3M-BSIP, a multimodal deep learning framework that predicts both the DNA-binding interface and residue-level base preference for DNA-binding proteins. It combines three protein representations, including a protein language model, to address the gap between the growing number of known proteins and the limited experimental characterization of their DNA-binding specificity. This offers a computational route to annotate binding specificity at scale.

papers.title: A compact generative language model learns the compositional grammar of phase-separating proteins.
papers.abstract: Liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) of intrinsically disordered proteins drives the formation of biomolecular condensates, yet the sequence-level grammar that promotes condensation remains difficult to specify from first principles. Existing protein language models are typically trained on large, folded-protein-rich sequence corpora and may not optimally capture the compositional biases of LLPS-prone disordered proteins. Here, we show that a compact generative language model, with an architecture and size (∼17 M parameters) selected via systematic hyperparameter optimization and cross-valida
papers.summary: The authors trained a compact generative language model (~17M parameters) specifically on phase-separating disordered proteins, showing that a small, well-tuned model can capture the compositional sequence grammar that drives liquid-liquid phase separation. This suggests that domain-specific, lightweight models can outperform larger general-purpose protein language models for disordered-protein tasks.

papers.title: Multiproperty optimization of therapeutic antibodies through sequence editing via large language model and reinforcement learning.
papers.abstract: Discovering antibodies with multiple beneficial properties is essential for therapeutic drug development, but experimentally identified antibodies require further optimization. Joint optimization remains challenging because sequence space is vast, annotations are sparse and property tradeoffs are common. Herein, we propose AbOptimizer, a reinforcement learning framework for multiproperty antibody optimization through parallel multisite sequence editing. AbOptimizer identifies promising editing sites and edit actions, including 'reservation', 'substitution' and optional 'insertion' or 'deletion
papers.summary: The authors present AbOptimizer, a reinforcement learning framework that uses a large language model to guide parallel edits at multiple sites in antibody sequences, aiming to improve several therapeutic properties simultaneously. The method identifies which positions to edit and what changes to make, including keeping, substituting, inserting, or deleting residues, to navigate the vast sequence space despite sparse annotations and property tradeoffs.

papers.title: Large language models poorly capture how word order shapes representations of sentence meaning in the human brain.
papers.abstract: Large language models based on the transformer architecture are now capable of producing human-like language. But do they encode and process linguistic meaning in a human-like way? Here, we address this question by analysing 7T fMRI data from 30 participants reading 108 sentences each. These sentences are carefully designed to disentangle sentence structure from word meaning, thereby testing whether transformer representations of sentence meaning resemble those formed by the brain. Using representational similarity analysis, we compared representations from eight transformers and eleven other
papers.summary: This study compared sentence representations from eight transformer-based large language models with 7T fMRI brain activity from 30 participants reading 108 carefully designed sentences. By disentangling word order from word meaning, the authors found that transformer models poorly capture how word order shapes neural representations of sentence meaning, suggesting LLMs do not process linguistic structure in a human-like way.

papers.title: BioHarness: Substrate-Aware Evidence Assembly for Biomedical Question Answering across Literature, Knowledge Bases, and Biological Atlases.
papers.abstract: Biomedical question answering often requires evidence beyond topically retrieved literature, including gene alias resolution, database identifier normalization, and atlas-derived biological measurements. However, existing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems typically follow a fixed workflow and lack an explicit mechanism for deciding when retrieved text is sufficient, when biomedical entity mapping is needed, or when executable evidence assembly over structured measurements should be invoked. This motivates a substrate-aware large language model (LLM) harness that selectively assemble
papers.summary: BioHarness is a large language model framework for biomedical question answering that decides when to rely on retrieved literature versus when to invoke entity mapping or executable queries over structured biological data such as knowledge bases and atlases. This substrate-aware approach moves beyond fixed retrieval-augmented generation workflows by selectively assembling evidence from multiple sources. It aims to improve answer accuracy for questions requiring gene alias resolution, identifier normalization, or atlas-derived measurements.

papers.title: Protein-Protein Interface Residue Prediction by Integrating Protein Language Representations and Structural Graph Attention.
papers.abstract: Accurate residue-level prediction of protein-protein interaction interfaces is important for elucidating molecular recognition mechanisms and guiding targeted drug design. However, interface residues are relatively sparse and governed by complex spatial dependencies, making their accurate identification challenging. In this study, we developed EvoStruct-GAT, a multimodal graph attention model based on the PDBbind v2020.R1 data set. To reduce information leakage arising from sequence homology, receptor and ligand sequences were clustered independently, and the resulting clusters were used to co
papers.summary: The authors present EvoStruct-GAT, a multimodal graph attention model that combines protein language model representations with structural graph features to predict which residues lie at protein-protein interfaces. They build the model on PDBbind v2020.R1 and control for sequence homology by clustering receptor and ligand sequences independently. The approach targets the sparse, spatially complex nature of interface residues to improve residue-level prediction for drug design applications.

papers.title: Machine Learning in Amyloidogenic Polypeptide Research: From Sequence Prediction to Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Over the past decade, machine learning (ML) has established a transformative paradigm for investigating amyloidogenic polypeptides. Characterized by their propensity to form ordered, β-sheet-rich fibrillar aggregates, these polypeptides are centrally implicated in the pathogenesis of numerous neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD). This review systematically evaluates the application of ML across critical domains of amyloid investigation: sequence-based amyloidogenicity prediction, structural biology, inhibitor design, and amyloid-related cl
papers.summary: This review surveys how machine learning has been applied across amyloid research, from predicting which protein sequences are likely to form amyloid fibrils to modeling their structures and designing inhibitor drugs. It frames ML as a transformative paradigm for studying amyloidogenic polypeptides implicated in Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases, organizing the field into sequence prediction, structural biology, and inhibitor design domains.

papers.title: Transformer Models in Vibrational Spectroscopy: A Review.
papers.abstract: Transformer models have attracted increasing interest in vibrational spectroscopy because of their ability to capture long-range dependencies in spectral data. These models have been applied to analytical tasks including spectral preprocessing, classification, quantitative analysis, multimodal data fusion, and spectra-to-structure prediction. Their flexible architectures support applications in Raman, infrared (IR), near-infrared (NIR), and surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS), with examples across chemistry, biology, and materials science. Transformer-based models also offer opportuniti
papers.summary: This review surveys the growing use of Transformer models in vibrational spectroscopy, covering tasks such as spectral preprocessing, classification, quantitative analysis, multimodal fusion, and spectra-to-structure prediction across Raman, IR, NIR, and SERS techniques. It highlights how Transformer architectures capture long-range dependencies in spectral data and support applications spanning chemistry, biology, and materials science.

papers.title: A multimodal deep learning model for classifying early- versus late-stage osteonecrosis of the femoral head on biparametric MRI.
papers.abstract: Precise early- versus late-stage stratification of osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) is critical for hip-preserving treatment selection, yet conventional MRI interpretation suffers from interobserver variability and limited objectivity. This study aimed to develop a multimodal deep learning model integrating biparametric MRI (STIR and T1-FSE) with clinical parameters (including age, sex, affected side (left, right, or bilateral), and etiology) to differentiate early- from late-stage ONFH and provide objective imaging evidence.
papers.summary: This study developed a multimodal deep learning model that combines biparametric MRI (STIR and T1-FSE sequences) with clinical parameters to classify early- versus late-stage osteonecrosis of the femoral head. The approach aims to reduce interobserver variability and provide objective imaging evidence for hip-preserving treatment decisions. The abstract describes the model's design but does not report performance results.

papers.title: AIDCare: A Technical Proof-of-Concept for Integrating Personalized Nutrition, Physical Activity, and AI-Assisted Care in Diabetes Lifestyle Management.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Medical nutrition therapy and structured lifestyle self-management are fundamental to diabetes care, yet conventional mobile health tools typically track diet, physical activity, and glucose measurements in isolation, with limited connection to clinical oversight. This study presents AIDCare, an integrated mobile health platform that connects camera-based nutritional assessment, wearable physical activity tracking, physiological monitoring, and clinician-supervised conversational artificial intelligence (AI) to support personalized dietary and lifestyle self-management i
papers.summary: AIDCare is a proof-of-concept mobile health platform that combines camera-based food recognition, wearable activity tracking, physiological monitoring, and a clinician-supervised conversational AI to support personalized diabetes lifestyle management. The work demonstrates technical integration of these components rather than reporting clinical outcomes, positioning it as an early-stage system design for connected diabetes care.

papers.title: Use of Demineralized Autologous Dentin Graft with the Tooth Processing Device in Immediate Post-Extraction Implant Placement and Loading: A 12-Month Evaluation of Peri-Implant Soft Tissue Stability.
papers.abstract: Purpose: To evaluate the effectiveness of immediate implant placement and loading combined with autologous dentin grafting in reducing post-extraction tissue remodelling, with particular emphasis on peri-implant soft tissue stability in the esthetic zone. Materials and Methods: This retrospective observational study included 13 patients (14 implant sites) with Type 1 extraction sockets in the anterior maxilla. Following atraumatic tooth extraction, implants were immediately placed and grafted with autologous dentin processed from the extracted tooth using the Tooth Transformer device. Screw-re
papers.summary: This retrospective study evaluated 13 patients (14 implant sites) who received immediate dental implants with autologous dentin grafts processed from their own extracted teeth using a Tooth Transformer device in the anterior maxilla. The 12-month follow-up focused on peri-implant soft tissue stability in the esthetic zone, suggesting the approach may help reduce post-extraction tissue remodeling. The small sample size and retrospective design limit the strength of the conclusions.

papers.title: FusionEP: Adaptive Cross-Modal Deep Fusion Network for Essential Protein Identification via Multi-Omics Integration and Contrastive Learning.
papers.abstract: Identifying essential proteins lays a foundation for dissecting disease mechanisms and mining therapeutic targets. Existing algorithms mostly adopt unimodal inputs and struggle to capture multi-level biological interactions from genomics, subcellular localization and proteomics. We present FusionEP, which is an adaptive cross-modal deep fusion network built upon contrastive learning to predict essential proteins. FusionEP integrates gene expression profiles, subcellular localization features, and protein interaction map structures. For gene expression information, we design a six-layer Transfo
papers.summary: FusionEP is a deep learning method that predicts essential proteins by combining gene expression, subcellular localization, and protein-protein interaction data through an adaptive cross-modal fusion network with contrastive learning. It aims to overcome the limitations of single-modality approaches that miss multi-level biological interactions. The work is a methodological contribution to computational essential protein identification, though its practical impact depends on benchmarking against existing tools.

papers.title: From Prediction to Generation: Artificial Intelligence Reconstructing the Paradigm of Protein Glycosylation Research.
papers.abstract: Among post-translational modifications, protein glycosylation is distinguished by its abundance and structural intricacy. Unlike protein biosynthesis, glycan assembly follows no template; it reflects glycosyltransferase/glycosidase competition, sugar-donor availability, and organelle-enforced compartmentalization, yielding heterogeneous glycoforms that confer functional versatility but complicate analysis. Three bottlenecks persist: stereochemical control in chemical glycosylation, ambiguous assignment of occupancy sites, and reproducing native conformations of fully glycosylated proteins. Ado
papers.summary: This review argues that artificial intelligence is shifting protein glycosylation research from prediction to generation, addressing three persistent bottlenecks: stereochemical control in chemical glycosylation, ambiguous assignment of glycosylation occupancy sites, and reproducing native conformations of fully glycosylated proteins. It surveys how AI methods can model the template-free, competition-driven nature of glycan assembly and generate glycoproteins rather than merely predict them.

papers.title: Relation-Aware Heterogeneous Graph Learning for miRNA-Drug Response Association Prediction Under Cold-Start Generalization.
papers.abstract: (1) Background: Cancer drug resistance can be influenced by microRNAs (miRNAs), which can alter gene expression and cellular pathways that determine how cancer cells respond to treatment. Potential miRNA-drug response associations can be identified using computational models; however, evaluating these models using edge-based evaluation can result in an optimistic view of model generalization since test miRNAs or drugs can appear in other response associations during training. (2) Methods: This paper presents a relation-aware heterogeneous learning framework that integrates miRNA expression pro
papers.summary: This paper introduces a relation-aware heterogeneous graph learning framework to predict associations between miRNAs and drug responses, addressing the problem of overoptimistic evaluation in existing computational models. By using cold-start generalization evaluation, where test miRNAs or drugs are entirely unseen during training, the method provides a more realistic assessment of predictive performance. The approach integrates miRNA expression profiles and relational graph structure to improve generalization to new miRNAs and drugs.

papers.title: Unlocking the Regulatory Genome by ARGUS: An Evidence-Constrained Agentic Framework for Interpreting Single Nucleotide Variants.
papers.abstract: Over 90% of disease-associated variants from genome-wide association studies fall in noncoding regulatory regions, yet their functional interpretation remains a central open problem in genomic medicine. Large language models prompted to interpret such variants routinely hallucinate transcription factor (TF) binding changes, fabricate experimental support, and assign biological significance to statistically negligible signals. We present ARGUS (Agentic Regulatory Genomics for an Uncertainty-aware Scientist), which strictly separates deterministic biological computation from LLM-mediated reasoni
papers.summary: ARGUS is an agentic framework that interprets noncoding single nucleotide variants by strictly separating deterministic biological computation (e.g., TF binding prediction, statistical testing) from LLM-mediated reasoning, aiming to prevent the hallucination and fabricated evidence common when LLMs are prompted directly. It constrains LLM outputs with computational evidence and uncertainty awareness, addressing the challenge that >90% of GWAS variants lie in regulatory regions.

papers.title: PepRePs: Peptide-Retargeted Phosphatases Designed with Generative Language Models.
papers.abstract: Phosphorylation is a fast, reversible layer of post-translational control that directly governs protein activity, signaling flux, and cell state. Kinases and phosphatases collectively establish these phosphorylation states, but their dysregulation drives cancer, neurodegenerative diseases, and developmental disorders. Selectively manipulating the phosphorylation of individual proteins in cells remains challenging, particularly for disordered substrates. Here, we introduce Peptide-Retargeted Phosphatases (PepRePs), a genetically encoded system that fuses a peptide binder to a serine/threonine p
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors introduce PepRePs, a genetically encoded system that retargets serine/threonine phosphatases to specific substrate proteins by fusing them to peptide binders. This enables selective manipulation of phosphorylation on individual proteins in cells, including disordered substrates that are otherwise difficult to target. The peptide binders were designed using generative language models, offering a new strategy for controlling signaling and cell state.

papers.title: iTB-DRS: a multi-stage feature selection framework to identify Mycobacterium tuberculosis drug-resistance using single-nucleotide polymorphisms.
papers.abstract: Rapid and accurate prediction of Mycobacterium tuberculosis drug resistance is crucial for effective tuberculosis control. However, data from genome-wide association studies are often characterized by high dimensionality and many redundant features, posing significant challenges to prediction models. To address these challenges, we propose a novel computational framework called iTB-DRS, which employs a hierarchical multi-stage feature selection strategy. The workflow begins with data encoding followed by a four-step selection mechanism, including (i) filtering noise using a Mean Decrease Accur
papers.summary: The authors present iTB-DRS, a computational framework that predicts Mycobacterium tuberculosis drug resistance from single-nucleotide polymorphisms using a hierarchical multi-stage feature selection strategy to handle high-dimensional, redundant genomic data. The four-step selection pipeline filters noise and reduces feature dimensionality before classification, aiming to improve resistance prediction accuracy. This is a methodological contribution to computational drug-resistance prediction rather than a new biological finding.

papers.title: Identification of plasma biomarkers for chronic kidney disease by integrating proteomics and machine learning.
papers.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major global health burden, and early identification of individuals at risk remains challenging. This study aimed to identify plasma proteomic biomarkers associated with incident CKD and develop a machine learning-based prediction model integrating proteomic and clinical data.
papers.summary: This study integrates plasma proteomics with machine learning to identify protein biomarkers associated with incident chronic kidney disease (CKD) and to build a prediction model combining proteomic and clinical data. The work aims to improve early identification of individuals at risk for CKD, addressing a major global health burden where early detection remains challenging.

papers.title: HiCP2GAN: a plug and play foundation model-based GAN for Hi-C enhancement.
papers.abstract: The 3D organization of chromatin shapes gene regulation and cellular function, and Hi-C has become the primary technique for mapping chromatin interactions genome-wide. However, high-resolution data remain costly and scarce, leaving many studies with sparse contact maps that limit downstream analysis. Deep learning methods, especially generative adversarial networks (GANs), have shown promise for enhancing low-resolution Hi-C data, but most existing GAN-based approaches rely on custom discriminators trained from scratch, which can yield unstable training and limited generalization. Hi-C founda
papers.summary: HiCP2GAN is a plug-and-play framework that uses a pretrained Hi-C foundation model as the discriminator in a GAN, rather than training a custom discriminator from scratch, to enhance low-resolution Hi-C contact maps. This leverages transferable chromatin-interaction representations to improve training stability and generalization for Hi-C resolution enhancement. The approach offers a practical way to recover higher-resolution chromatin contact information from sparse, low-cost Hi-C data.

papers.title: AxialTAD: an axial contrast architecture for TAD boundary prediction from Hi-C.
papers.abstract: Topologically associating domains (TADs) are fundamental units of 3D chromatin organization, and accurate identification of TAD boundaries from Hi-C contact matrices remains an active challenge. Recent deep learning approaches have advanced substantially, but these rely on increasingly large architectures, raising the question of how much of this capacity boundary-centric analysis requires. Here we propose AxialTAD, a compact deep learning model centered on an Axial Contrast Module (ACM) that explicitly encodes directional contrast in contact intensity along the row and column axes of local Hi
papers.summary: AxialTAD is a compact deep learning model for predicting TAD boundaries from Hi-C contact matrices. Its key innovation is an Axial Contrast Module that explicitly encodes directional contrast in contact intensity along row and column axes of local Hi-C patches, achieving competitive boundary prediction with a much smaller architecture than recent large models. The work suggests that boundary-centric analysis does not require the massive capacity of current deep learning approaches.

papers.title: Deciphering Host Genomic Pathway Landscapes in Severe COVID-19 by Exome Sequencing of a Large Admixed Brazilian Cohort.
papers.abstract: The host genetic factors that resulted in the heterogeneous clinical outcomes of COVID-19 remained poorly understood, especially in admixed populations that are underrepresented in global genomic studies. In this study, we investigated the genetic landscape associated with COVID-19 severity using whole-exome sequencing data from 325 Brazilian individuals recruited between 2020 and 2023. To prioritize variants related to disease severity, we applied a machine learning framework combining Support Vector Machine - Recursive Feature Elimination and SHAP interpretation. This approach encompasses 25
papers.summary: This study performed whole-exome sequencing on 325 admixed Brazilian COVID-19 patients and used a machine learning pipeline (SVM-RFE with SHAP interpretation) to prioritize host genetic variants associated with disease severity. The work highlights pathway-level genetic contributions to severe COVID-19 in an underrepresented, admixed population, addressing a gap in global genomic studies that have largely focused on European-ancestry cohorts.

papers.title: Interpretable Drug-Target Prediction via Geometric Alignment: A Linear Alternative to Deep Architectural Complexity.
papers.abstract: Designing selective kinase inhibitors is a multiobjective optimization problem constrained by the structural conservation of the human kinome, along with the lack of high-quality interaction data. Traditional deep learning methods often train complex neural networks directly on small datasets and fail to generalize to new chemical scaffolds. To this end, we present Geometric Manifold Alignment, a novel linear approach that shifts away from architectural complexity. We introduce Multi-View Linear Manifold (MVLM), which aligns the latent spaces of ChemBERTa (small molecules) and ESM-2 (protein s
papers.summary: The authors propose Multi-View Linear Manifold (MVLM), a linear method that aligns latent embeddings from ChemBERTa (compounds) and ESM-2 (proteins) to predict kinase inhibitor targets. They argue this geometric alignment approach generalizes better to novel chemical scaffolds than complex deep learning models trained on small interaction datasets, offering an interpretable alternative to deep architectural complexity.

papers.title: A Scalable Workflow for Extracting Species Interactions From Ecological Literature Using Large Language Models.
papers.abstract: The contemporary ecological crisis calls for integration and synthesis of vast amounts of mostly scattered and often hard-to-extract ecological information that is dispersed across hundreds of thousands of scientific papers. Recent advancements in natural language processing (NLP) and the emergence of large language models (LLMs) offer a novel and promising approach to this persistent challenge. Here, we present a replicable and adaptable workflow that automates the extraction of a broad range of biological interactions among species from scientific literature using LLMs. We provide a demonstr
papers.summary: The authors present a replicable, adaptable workflow that uses large language models to automatically extract species interaction data from ecological literature, addressing the challenge of synthesizing scattered information across hundreds of thousands of papers. They demonstrate the approach on a dataset, showing that LLM-based extraction can automate a task that has traditionally required manual curation. This offers a scalable path toward building large ecological interaction databases.

papers.title: MGP_HNSC32: A H&E Morphology-Derived 32-Gene Prognostic Signature in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSC) exhibits substantial molecular and morphological heterogeneity, yet current morphology-based prognostic models often lack biological interpretability. We developed a transformer-based computational framework (CTransPath) to virtually predict gene expression directly from hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) whole-slide images. Morphology-associated genes were identified from the TCGA-HNSC cohort, and a 32-gene morphology-guided prognostic signature (MGP_HNSC32) based on H&E-derived predicted gene expression was developed using Random Survival Forest and mult
papers.summary: The authors built a transformer-based model (CTransPath) that predicts gene expression directly from H&E whole-slide images in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, then used the predicted expression to derive a 32-gene prognostic signature (MGP_HNSC32) via Random Survival Forest. This links tumor morphology to molecular prognosis, offering a more interpretable alternative to purely image-based prognostic models.

papers.title: A hybrid CNN-BiLSTM network with additive attention for automated four-stage classification of Alzheimer's disease from brain MRI.
papers.abstract: AD is a progressive and irreversible neurodegenerative disorder. Because the structural changes that accompany the earliest stages of the disease are subtle and easily overlooked, manual interpretation of MRI is time-consuming and prone to inter-observer disagreement. This study presents an end-to-end deep learning framework that fuses spatial and sequential reasoning to classify brain MRI into four clinically meaningful stages: Person with no dementia, Person with very mild dementia, Person with mild dementia, and Person with moderate dementia. An additive attention mechanism subsequently wei
papers.summary: This paper presents a hybrid deep learning model combining convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) and additive attention to classify brain MRI scans into four stages of Alzheimer's disease, from no dementia to moderate dementia. The approach aims to automate staging and reduce reliance on time-consuming, subjective manual MRI interpretation. The abstract is truncated, so reported performance metrics are not available.

papers.title: Pathology-guided multimodal transformer predicts postoperative survival benefit from adjuvant chemotherapy in glioma: from DNA damage repair to immune characterization.
papers.abstract: High-grade gliomas (HGGs) are aggressive primary brain tumors with high recurrence rates and poor prognosis. Survival benefit from adjuvant temozolomide (TMZ) varies substantially across patients, and reliable preoperative biomarkers for treatment stratification remain limited. This study aims to develop an interpretable multimodal deep learning model integrating whole-slide histopathological images and multiparametric MRI to preoperatively predict survival benefit from adjuvant TMZ in HGG patients.
papers.summary: This study develops a multimodal deep learning model that combines whole-slide pathology images and MRI scans to predict, before surgery, which high-grade glioma patients will benefit from adjuvant temozolomide chemotherapy. The model is designed to be interpretable and links predictions to DNA damage repair and immune characteristics.

papers.title: Systemic immune dysregulation and local barrier failure as predictors of septic shock in acute appendicitis: a large-scale multicenter interpretable machine learning study.
papers.abstract: The transition from localized acute appendicitis to systemic septic shock is driven by complex immune and metabolic dysregulation combined with anatomical barrier failure. Accurately predicting early hemodynamic deterioration remains clinically challenging. This study aimed to develop an interpretable multimodal machine learning model by integrating systemic immunological profiles with local sonographic characteristics.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This multicenter study develops an interpretable multimodal machine learning model that combines systemic immunological profiles with local sonographic features to predict progression from acute appendicitis to septic shock. The work aims to enable earlier identification of hemodynamic deterioration by capturing both immune dysregulation and anatomical barrier failure.

papers.title: Global thyroid cancer incidence in relation to dietary and socioeconomic factors: an ecological machine learning study.
papers.abstract: Thyroid cancer incidence has risen dramatically worldwide, with marked geographic heterogeneity suggesting dietary and environmental contributions beyond screening effects. The roles of specific dietary patterns in thyroid cancer remain poorly characterized at the global level.
papers.summary: This ecological study uses machine learning to relate global thyroid cancer incidence to dietary and socioeconomic factors across countries. It finds that dietary patterns and socioeconomic indicators are associated with geographic variation in thyroid cancer incidence, though the ecological design cannot establish causality. The work highlights diet and socioeconomic context as candidate contributors to the worldwide rise in thyroid cancer.

papers.title: Gradient boosting models for gallstone disease classification: A comparative study using demographic and clinical data.
papers.abstract: Gallstone disease is a prevalent gastrointestinal condition with a substantial healthcare burden. While abdominal ultrasonography is the established first-line diagnostic modality, opportunistic risk stratification using routinely collected health parameters remains underexplored. This study evaluated the discriminatory capacity of four gradient boosting machine learning algorithms (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, and HistGBM) for classifying gallstone status using demographic, bioimpedance, and routine laboratory features. A retrospective clinical dataset of 319 patients (161 gallstone-positive
papers.summary: This study compared four gradient boosting machine learning algorithms (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, HistGBM) for classifying gallstone disease using demographic, bioimpedance, and routine laboratory data from 319 patients. The work evaluates whether routinely collected health parameters can support opportunistic risk stratification as a complement to ultrasound diagnosis. It is a comparative modeling study on a modest single-center retrospective cohort.

papers.title: Routine Metabolic Laboratory Profile and Time-Stratified Machine-Learning Risk Stratification of Rosacea: A Combined Retrospective-Prospective Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Rosacea has been linked with systemic metabolic abnormalities in case-control studies, but most such evidence compares rosacea patients with healthy controls rather than asking which patients within a rosacea population carry the greatest metabolic burden. We aimed to describe the metabolic profile of a real-world rosacea outpatient cohort and build a time-stratified, outcome-independent machine-learning model ranking which routine metabolic indicators predict metabolic syndrome status.
papers.summary: This study characterizes the metabolic profile of a real-world rosacea outpatient cohort and develops a time-stratified machine-learning model to rank routine metabolic indicators by their ability to predict metabolic syndrome status within rosacea patients. Rather than comparing rosacea patients to healthy controls, it focuses on stratifying metabolic risk within the rosacea population itself.

papers.title: A fuzzy-augmented deep learning pipeline for multilingual natural language processing from handwritten script: a Tamil case study.
papers.abstract: Multilingual natural language processing (NLP) from handwritten script is an open artificial intelligence (AI) challenge requiring advances in both pattern recognition and sequence generation. Existing end-to-end pipelines often fail to model the structural uncertainty in complex scripts, particularly the decorative stroke variability in Dravidian writing systems, before passing representations to downstream NLP models. This omission can result in error propagation from the recognition stage into translation. This paper proposes a Tamil Handwritten Character Recognition and Translation (THCRT)
papers.summary: The paper proposes THCRT, a fuzzy-augmented deep learning pipeline for recognizing handwritten Tamil characters and translating them into natural language. It aims to model structural uncertainty in decorative stroke variability before passing representations to downstream NLP models, reducing error propagation from recognition to translation. The work is a case study for multilingual NLP from handwritten scripts.

papers.title: Virology-aware artificial intelligence for respiratory antiviral discovery: from molecular docking biases to RdRp-centered benchmarking.
papers.abstract: Respiratory RNA viruses remain a persistent threat because they combine high transmissibility, rapid evolution, immune escape, zoonotic spillover, and incomplete therapeutic coverage. RNA-dependent RNA polymerases (RdRps) and polymerase complexes are among the most conserved and pharmacologically actionable viral targets, yet they are also challenging computational targets because their ligandable states depend on RNA templates, cofactors, divalent metals, multidomain architecture, and conformational transitions. Artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), geometri
papers.summary: This review argues that AI-driven discovery of respiratory antivirals must be designed around the specific biology of RNA-dependent RNA polymerases (RdRps), rather than relying on generic docking pipelines that introduce systematic biases. The authors trace how RdRp ligandability depends on RNA templates, metal cofactors, and conformational states, and propose RdRp-centered benchmarking to make AI predictions more reliable for this target class.

papers.title: A Two-Stage ESM-Based Machine Learning Pipeline for Robust Hierarchically Evaluated Enzyme Function Prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate enzyme annotation remains a major bottleneck in translating rapidly growing protein sequence data into biological knowledge. Enzyme Commission (EC) prediction is particularly challenging because enzyme functions are organized hierarchically, annotations are often imbalanced across classes, and sequence similarity alone may be insufficient to resolve functional differences. To address these challenges, we developed ESM-ECForest, a 2-stage framework that combines protein embeddings generated by the pretrained language model ESM-2 (Evolutionary Scale Modeling 2) with random forest classi
papers.summary: The authors present ESM-ECForest, a two-stage machine learning pipeline that uses protein language model embeddings (ESM-2) combined with random forest classifiers to predict Enzyme Commission (EC) numbers. The framework is designed to handle the hierarchical organization of enzyme functions and class imbalance, aiming to improve annotation accuracy beyond sequence-similarity-based approaches.

papers.title: Routine laboratory biomarker signature combined with machine learning for rapid differentiation of intracerebral hemorrhage from acute ischemic stroke.
papers.abstract: Rapid and reliable differentiation between intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and acute ischemic stroke (IS) is essential for appropriate triage and treatment. We aimed to develop and validate a laboratory-based machine learning model using routine clinical chemistry and hematology parameters to discriminate ICH from IS.
papers.summary: This study develops and validates a machine learning model that uses routine clinical chemistry and hematology parameters to distinguish intracerebral hemorrhage from acute ischemic stroke. The approach aims to support rapid triage and treatment decisions without relying on neuroimaging.

papers.title: Ordinal measurement invariance of three retained GAEU-1 dimensions in Chilean and Ecuadorian university samples.
papers.abstract: Meaningful cross-national comparisons of self-regulated learning (SRL), motivation, and related learning-regulation constructs require evidence that the measurement model operates comparably across groups. We tested this requirement for three GAEU-1 dimensions previously retained in Chile and Ecuador using the open Version-5 dataset (N = 1,316; Chile n = 631; Ecuador n = 685). Fifteen ordered indicators representing the GAEU-1 SRL factor, conscious motivational strategies, and deep learning techniques were analyzed with WLSMV, followed by a Wu-Estabrook multigroup ordinal invariance sequence a
papers.summary: This study tested whether three dimensions of the GAEU-1 instrument (self-regulated learning, conscious motivational strategies, and deep learning techniques) measure the same constructs equivalently in Chilean and Ecuadorian university students. Using ordinal measurement invariance analysis (WLSMV with a Wu-Estabrook multigroup sequence) on 1,316 respondents, the authors assessed cross-national comparability of the measurement model. The work provides evidence relevant to whether meaningful cross-national comparisons of these learning-regulation constructs are valid.

papers.title: Integrated bioinformatics and machine learning identify key hub genes in early-onset gastric cancer.
papers.abstract: Early-onset gastric cancer (EOGC) represents a clinically and biologically distinct subtype of gastric cancer characterized by unique molecular features. However, its underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to identify EOGC-associated hub genes using an integrated bioinformatics and machine learning framework.
papers.summary: This study applies an integrated bioinformatics and machine learning pipeline to identify hub genes associated with early-onset gastric cancer (EOGC), a clinically distinct subtype with poorly understood molecular mechanisms. By combining differential expression analysis with machine learning-based feature selection, the authors nominate candidate hub genes that may serve as biomarkers or therapeutic targets for EOGC. The work is exploratory and will require experimental validation to confirm biological relevance.

papers.title: BKPyVN-associated macrophage subpopulations and diagnostic biomarker identification - combine machine learning with single-cell analysis.
papers.abstract: As pivotal effector cells of innate immunity, macrophages may play a critical role in immune regulation and fibrotic remodeling in BK polyomavirus nephropathy (BKPyVN) following kidney transplantation. However, their subpopulation heterogeneity, molecular characteristics, and functional mechanisms remain poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study combines single-cell transcriptomics with machine learning to characterize macrophage subpopulations in BK polyomavirus nephropathy (BKPyVN) after kidney transplantation. The authors identify distinct macrophage states associated with immune regulation and fibrotic remodeling, and propose candidate diagnostic biomarkers derived from these subpopulations. The work is exploratory and biomarker candidates require independent validation.

papers.title: Research progress on the application of multi-scale computational methods in the research and development of anti-tuberculosis infection drugs.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), driven by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), remains a leading cause of mortality from infectious disease worldwide.​ The global dissemination of multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) strains-coupled with protracted treatment regimens and the persistence of latent infection-has not only compromised first-line chemotherapies but also underscored the stagnation of conventional drug development pipelines. In this review, we systematically synthesize how multi-scale computational strategies are reshaping anti-TB drug discovery and explicitly delineate the
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how multi-scale computational strategies—spanning molecular modeling, network analysis, and systems-level approaches—are being applied to anti-tuberculosis drug discovery. It highlights how these methods address the stagnation of conventional pipelines amid rising multidrug-resistant and extensively drug-resistant Mtb strains, and outlines their role in targeting latent infection and shortening treatment regimens.

papers.title: Biophysics-informed computational framework for predicting antisense oligonucleotide knockdown efficacy under small-data constraints.
papers.abstract: A central strategy in treating neurodegenerative disorders, including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), is lowering levels of disease-driving proteins. Antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) offer a direct RNA-targeted approach to reduce protein expression, but experimental discovery and optimization are constrained by small, heterogeneous datasets and target-specific variability. Computational models that predict ASO knockdown efficacy directly from sequence and context could improve candidate selection, yet generalization across gene families and experimental settings remains challenging. In t
papers.summary: The authors present a biophysics-informed computational framework for predicting how effectively antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) reduce target RNA/protein levels, specifically designed to work with the small, heterogeneous datasets typical of ASO development for neurodegenerative diseases like ALS. By incorporating biophysical principles into the model, the approach aims to improve generalization across different gene families and experimental conditions where purely data-driven models struggle.

papers.title: Identification of SLC15A3 as a shared prognostic biomarker for AML and COVID-19 via integrative bioinformatics, machine learning and Mendelian randomization.
papers.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a lethal hematological malignancy with poor overall prognosis.COVID-19 co-infection further complicates clinical management and worsens survival outcomes of AML patients, highlighting the need to explore the molecular interplay between the two diseases. In this study, we initially screened 109 common differentially expressed genes shared by AML and COVID-19 from public transcriptomic datasets, which were closely involved in tumor progression and viral pathogenesis. We further characterized their biological functions, constructed protein interaction and TF-miRNA
papers.summary: This study integrated public transcriptomic datasets, machine learning, and Mendelian randomization to identify SLC15A3 as a gene whose expression is shared between acute myeloid leukemia and COVID-19, proposing it as a prognostic biomarker for both conditions. The authors screened 109 common differentially expressed genes and characterized their functions and regulatory networks. The work is exploratory and relies on computational reanalysis of existing data without experimental validation.

papers.title: Transcriptomic identification of high-altitude illness candidate genes and physiological mechanisms: a multidimensional bioinformatics study with 106 drug-food homologous substance target prediction.
papers.abstract: High-altitude (HA) illness threatens health after acute high-altitude exposure, but its molecular mechanisms and effective interventions remain unclear. Drug-food homologous (DFH) substances have potential for HA illness intervention, yet their active components and targets are unknown.
papers.summary: This study uses transcriptomic and bioinformatics analyses to identify candidate genes and physiological mechanisms underlying high-altitude illness, then predicts targets of 106 drug-food homologous substances that might intervene. It is an exploratory computational study that proposes candidate genes and intervention targets but does not experimentally validate them.

papers.title: Computational approaches to deep learning-driven EEG analysis for neurological disease diagnosis: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is a widely used non-invasive neurophysiological technique for analyzing brain dynamics and diagnosing neurological diseases. However, the non-stationary nature, low signal-to-noise ratio, and inter-subject variability of EEG signals cause significant challenges to traditional analytical approaches. In recent years, deep learning has emerged as a powerful computational tool for EEG analysis, which enables automated feature learning and improved diagnostic accuracy with minimal human-driven feature extraction. This review systematically explains computational approa
papers.summary: This systematic review surveys computational approaches that apply deep learning to EEG analysis for diagnosing neurological diseases. It explains how deep learning enables automated feature learning and improved diagnostic accuracy despite challenges like non-stationarity, low signal-to-noise ratio, and inter-subject variability in EEG signals.

papers.title: Protective effects of testosterone replacement therapy on brain tumor outcomes: The Mayo Clinic experience.
papers.abstract: Biological sex and endocrine signaling influence cancer biology, immune response, and therapeutic outcomes. Recent evidence suggests that testosterone signaling may exert brain-context-dependent protective effects in glioblastoma (GBM) through the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, reduced glucocorticoid-mediated immune suppression, and altered tumor-immune interactions. We assessed whether testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) exposure was associated with survival in solid tumor central nervous system (CNS) metastases and glioblastoma (GBM, IDH-wildtype, WHO grade 4), settings in which pos
papers.summary: This Mayo Clinic study examined whether testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) is associated with survival outcomes in patients with glioblastoma and solid tumor CNS metastases. The findings suggest TRT exposure may have protective effects on brain tumor outcomes, potentially through endocrine and immune mechanisms such as reduced glucocorticoid-mediated immune suppression. The work highlights biological sex and endocrine signaling as factors influencing brain cancer biology and therapeutic response.

papers.title: Evaluation of large language models for ICI-related liver injury with an emerging microbiome focus.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-related liver injury (ICI-LI) has heterogeneous phenotypes, a complex differential diagnosis, and evolving management. Gut microbiome research provides biological plausibility for immune regulation during ICI therapy, but evidence specific to ICI-LI remains limited and is not yet clinically actionable. We evaluated whether publicly accessible large language model (LLM) chatbots can organize this mixed evidence base and communicate its uncertainty.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study evaluates whether publicly accessible LLM chatbots can accurately organize and communicate the mixed evidence base on immune checkpoint inhibitor-related liver injury (ICI-LI), including its heterogeneous phenotypes, complex differential diagnosis, and evolving management. It also examines how well these models convey the limited and not-yet-clinically-actionable microbiome evidence relevant to ICI-LI. The work assesses LLM utility for synthesizing uncertain clinical evidence in a niche immuno-oncology context.
